does: Breaks soft, cooked flesh into a rough, stringy mash with a fork, so that some texture is left and the smoky taste of the food is not lost to a machine.
how: Make sure the flesh is completely soft, and let any bitter juice drain off.
Put the flesh in a bowl and press and drag a fork through it until it falls into strands and small soft lumps.
Stir in the dressing a little at a time as you go, so that the flesh takes up the seasoning.
Stop while some texture is left.

cues.text: Rough strands and small soft lumps, not a smooth paste.
No firm bits left under the fork.

mistakes.mistake: Blending it to a smooth paste, so that the texture is lost.
mistakes.fix: Use a fork, and stop while strands are still showing.

mistakes.mistake: Mashing flesh that is not soft all the way, which leaves hard bits.
mistakes.fix: Keep it on the heat until it has collapsed completely.

comes_after.why: The flesh is soft and smoky from the flame before it is mashed.

variant_of.differs: The flesh is broken into a rough, stringy mass by hand and not beaten smooth, and no butter or milk goes in.
